monsters.name: Boss BloodMoon
monsters.note: A monster literally named after the server. Distinct MonsterClass (802) from Boss Farao (801), but its EventItemBag reward-config file is byte-identical to Boss Farao's, INCLUDING an internal EventName field that still reads "Boss Farao" and an empty item-reward section. This looks like an in-progress custom boss: the entity was allocated its own class/index, but its reward configuration was copy-pasted from Farao's template and not yet customized. Both files share the exact same file-system LastWriteTimeUtc (2026-08-15), suggesting both were created/touched in the same batch operation.

mapMonsterItemChain.description: The closest thing to a full verified MAP -> MONSTER -> ITEM chain found this round (Part M).
mapMonsterItemChain.chain: MAP-1 --HOSTS_WAVE--> MonsterIndex 55 (Skeleton King) spawns at (78,191) --SAME_COORDS_AS--> a 100%-rate drop of Type14/Index8 (cure item) at (78,191)
mapMonsterItemChain.factStatus: FACT (each individual data point -- the map, the monster spawn coordinates, the item drop coordinates -- is read directly from the real config)
mapMonsterItemChain.inferenceStatus: INFERENCE (that the monster's death is what CAUSES the item drop). The config's drop section is structured as a location+rate+item entry, not an explicit 'this monster drops this item' relationship -- it is highly plausible this is a kill-triggered drop given the exact coordinate match with the wave-3 spawn point, but the file does not explicitly say 'MonsterIndex 55 drops ItemType 14/Index 8 on death.' A different plausible reading: this could be a location-based pickup independent of any specific kill. Recorded as INFERENCE, not FACT, per the required FACT/INFERENCE/RECOMMENDATION separation.
mapMonsterItemChain.notAFullChain: This is a MAP->MONSTER + MAP->ITEM(same-location) pairing, not a config-explicit MONSTER->DROPS_ITEM edge. No fully unambiguous MAP->MONSTER->ITEM chain (where the source text itself states the monster-to-item drop relationship) was found in this pass.
